sentences.text:
Municipal Council Of Bhiwani vs The State Of Haryana on 15
February, 2024
Bench: Hrishikesh Roy, Prashant Kumar Mishra

In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2024
 (Arising Out Of Slp (Criminal) No. 6335 Of 2019)
 Municipal Council Of Bhiwani (Haryana) Appella
 Versus
 The State Of Haryana & Anr.

Respond
 O R D E R
Leave granted.
2. Heard Mr. Prabhoo Dayal Tiwari, learned counsel appearing for the appellant  Municipal Council, Bhiwani.
The State of Haryana is represented by Mr. Deepak Thukral, learned AAG.
The respondent No. 2 (accused No. 1 in the FIR No. 40 of 2010) has filed counter affidavit but none appears from his side.

3. The respondent No. 2 filed the CRM-M No. 25502 of 2011 (O&M) before the High Court and when the case was listed on 06.02.2019, the counsel for the appellant stated that he wished to withdraw the petition reserving the right to file a fresh one.
The Court permitted the withdrawal and passed appropriate order.
Surprisingly, although the petition was dismissed as withdrawn, the Court went on to pass a substantial order to the following effect:
However, it is made clear that till then the trial Court shall not proceed ahead into the trial.

4. Mr. Tiwari would point out that the FIR in the case was filed by the Executive Officer of the Municipal Council after noticing 13:21:20 IST Reason:
that there was tampering in the entries in the concerned assessment registers of the Municipal Council.
The concerned entries were interpolated by the co-accused Ashok Kumar, who was a Clerk in the Municipal Council, to benefit the accused No. 1 - Bhupinder Singh.
The chargesheet against the accused was filed under Sections 420, 466, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC.

sentences.text:
The records show that the respondent No. 2 filed the petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with the following prayer:
It is, therefore, respectfully prayed that record of the case be perused and after perusal of the same, the FIR No. 40 dated 03.03.2010 under Sections 420, 466, 467,
468, 471, 120B IPC Police Station Civil Lines, Bhiwani, Distt. Bhiwani (Annexure P/2) along with entire subsequent proceedings undertaken in pursuance therefore including report under Section 173 Cr.P.C. (Annexure P/3) may kindly be ordered to be quashed, in the interest of justice.
6.

Having regard to the aforesaid prayer in the quashing petition and the said petition having been dismissed by the High Court on 06.02.2019, there should have been no occasion for the learned Judge to pass any order stalling the trial.

7. The respondent No. 2 as the accused No. 1, is the beneficiary of the above order and although a counter affidavit was filed on his behalf, nothing is said in the said counter affidavit on how the impugned order of the High Court is justified.
The counsel for the respondent No. 2 is not present in Court to justify the order.
8. The learned AAG in his turn submits that stay of trial should not have been ordered by the High Court when the quashing petition of the accused No. 1 was dismissed as withdrawn.
9. Having considered the above and finding that there is no justification to stay the trial, we deem it appropriate to set aside the impugned order dated 06.02.2019.
The appeal is allowed with this order.

10. The Registry should furnish a copy of this order to the learned AAG and also forward a copy to the concerned Court so that all are informed that there is no impediment to proceed with the trial in the case arising out of the FIR No. 40 of 2010 registered at the Police Station Bhiwani.
11. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.
..................J. (HRISHIKESH ROY) ..................J. (PRASHANT KUMAR MISHRA) NEW DELHI;
FEBRUARY 15, 2024.
